memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Moses used to take a tent and pitch it outside the camp some distance away, calling it the 'tent of meeting'. Anyone enquiring of the Lord would go to the tent of meeting outside the camp." - Exod 33:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This tent is not yet the tabernacle. It is a simple arrangement Moses made — a tent pitched at a distance, where God could be sought.

Two details matter. First, it was outside the camp. Sin had created distance, and the tent's location made that visible. Second, anyone could come. It was not reserved for Moses. Any Israelite who wanted to seek the Lord could walk out there and do so.

That combination — real distance, and a real way to draw near — is the story of the whole Bible in miniature.

Hebrews takes up this very picture and turns it: Jesus suffered outside the city gate, and we are called to go out to Him, bearing the disgrace He bore (Heb 13:12-13). The place of meeting with God is now a Person, and He met us outside the camp.

Here is the beautiful reversal: because Christ went outside, we are brought inside. The curtain is torn (Heb 10:19-20). We do not walk to a tent in the desert; we come with confidence to the throne of grace.

But this still asks something of us. Moses had to walk out there deliberately. Meeting with God rarely happens by accident.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you have a habit and a place of meeting with God?
2. What distractions keep you from seeking Him deliberately?
3. What does it mean to you that Christ suffered outside the gate?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that the way to You is open through Jesus. Give me a hunger to seek You daily. Amen.
